description.narrative:
OXFAM in LAOS and Oxfam in Asia aspires to drive the private sector and policy makers in Asia to initiate key steps for policy improvement relating to fair value chains, with the emphasis on labour rights and gender equality by engaging with CSOs, workers, farmers, and women groups. It has collaborated with national programme teams and local partners to bring forward the propositions and voices of the civil society to ASEAN high-level space on the inclusive and responsible business (IRB) agenda. Oxfam has been invited to participate in the ASEAN IB process since its inaugural forum. This year, the Lao government is holding the 2024 ASEAN chairmanship.For the same purpose, since early 2024 Oxfam in Laos (OiL) has approached and engaged with Lao PDR's Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MIC) for Oxfam ‘s participation in the 7th ASEAN IB Forum in September 2024. Objectives 1. To showcase models on how IB can contribute to addressing unpaid care and domestic work (UCDW), strengthening social protection (SP), promoting women’s economic empowerment (WEE), and enabling climate resilience, where recommendations can be distilled for consideration in the ASEAN accreditation standards for IB. 2. To promote and enhance the position of Oxfam in Laos, its national programme works, and its relationship with relevant Lao PDR’s official agencies for its works around care economy, gender empowerment, and enterprise development, to support OiL’sfuture works and engagement in the country. Expected Outcomes 1. Oxfam’s continued engagement and presence at the annual ASEAN Inclusive Business Summit/Forum, both to affirm Oxfam’s commitment to support the ASEAN and its member states in promoting inclusive andresponsible business standards in the region and advocate its IRB propositions to ASEAN. 2. Relationship building with ASEAN to maintain Oxfam’s access to this regional policy and advocacy space and nurture foundation for future engagement at the next IB Summit during Malaysia’s ASEAN chairmanship in 2025 and the Philippines’ chairmanship in 2026. Outputs 1. Partial (funding, logistical and procurement) support to the Lao PDR’s government’s organization of the 7th ASEAN IBF. 2. Sharing of Oxfam and networks’ experience oninclusive and responsible business (IRB) to ASEAN member states and the event participants. 3. Media coverage of Oxfam’s engagementwith ASEAN and Oxfam’s IRB propositions. Oxfam’s proposed engagement Tentative agreement between OiL and the Lao MIC for Oxfam’s participation in the formal programme of the 7th ASEAN IBF, based on the current version of the agenda enclosed which has been endorsed by the ASEAN Coordinating Committee on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ACCMSME), is as following. 1. John Samuel, Oxfam Asia Regional Director, to speak: a. On Day 1 during the ‘Opening Ceremony’ from 09.00 - 09.30 hrs. on Monday 23 September 2024. b. On Day 2 during the ‘Closing remarks’ from 12.00 - 12.30 hrs. on Tuesday 24 September 2024. 2. Oxfam to nominate a panel speaker to join Day 1 session ‘Beyond ASEAN – Other experiences promoting inclusive businesses and the social economy’ from 15.15-16.45 hrs. on Monday 23 September 2024. Oxfam can bring in speaker(s) with different experiences and strengths from other countries in promoting inclusive businesses, drawing from both its own works and its global networks of both MSME partners and the private sector. Approach Oxfam’s participation in the 7th ASEAN IBF will be mainly led by OiL with the Lao PDR’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with support from the Advocacy <(>&<)> Campaign Team of the Asia Regional Platform. OiL will undertake all procurement directly and comply with its relevant financial and logistic requirements and systems. Timeline The 7th ASEAN IBF will take place from Monday 23 – Tuesday 24September 2024 for 1.5 days at Lao Plaza Hotel, Vientiane. The pre-event preparation and post-event works including expense clearing and final reporting should take 4 months maximum from August – November 2024.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
